title: Aaron and Bryce Dessner Celebrate Their 50th Birthdays with Michael Stipe, The N
content:
In a distinctive celebration of their 50th birthdays, twin brothers Aaron and Bryce Dessner, best known for their roles as guitarists in The National, headlined a series of collaborative events across Europe. These performances combined personal milestones with artistic reunions and unique live interpretations, underscoring the brothers’ influential presence in indie and alternative music.

The festivities unfolded over two days, centered around the AB100 event hosted at Teatro Kursaal in San Sebastian, Spain. This marked The National’s sole scheduled appearance for 2026 and their first live show since 2024. The concert featured a rich blend of familiar collaborators and special guests, delivering a diverse musical program that honored the Dessners’ careers and friendships.

Early in the evening, Richard Reed Parry of Arcade Fire, a longtime collaborator with The National, joined the band on stage for renditions of "Lemonworld" and "Bloodbuzz Ohio." These performances set the tone for a night that balanced deep cuts with celebrated hits. One particularly notable moment was the inclusion of Icelandic artist Ragnar Kjartansson, who revisited his past collaboration with the band from the 2013 multimedia project "A Lot of Sorrow." In homage to that extensive six-hour performance of the song "Sorrow," The National performed the track twice consecutively, complemented by the original visual installation.

Further enriching the show, vocal contributions came from singers Lisa Hannigan, Kate Stables, and Mina Tindle, the latter being Bryce Dessner’s spouse. Their harmonies on "Oblivions" added a layered vocal texture. The evening culminated with a communal sing-along of "Vanderlyle Crybaby Geeks," a fan favorite from the acclaimed "High Violet" album, involving friends and family who had gathered for the AB100 celebrations.

Adding to the evening’s rarity, The National resurrected "90-Mile Water Wall," a song from their 2003 release "Sad Songs for Dirty Lovers," which had not been performed live since mid-2014. This choice highlighted the band’s willingness to venture beyond their standard setlist and reflect on their extensive catalog.

Prior to the San Sebastian event, the Dessners orchestrated a gathering in Biarritz, France, called Mixtape, where they shared the stage with artists such as Ben Howard, Kevin Morby, and Jon Hopkins. The surprise guest for the night was Michael Stipe, the former R.E.M. frontman, who performed his track "E-Bow the Letter" from the 1996 album "New Adventures in Hi-Fi," as well as "No Time for Love Like Now," a piece co-created with Aaron’s Big Red Machine project in 2020.

The presence of "E-Bow the Letter" carried additional resonance, given its origins in San Sebastian and its historical significance for the involved musicians. Aaron Dessner recalled their attempts to have R.E.M. perform the song during earlier tours, underscoring the deep artistic ties between the collaborators. Notably, Stipe’s last live rendition of the song was in 2009 during R.E.M.’s final public performance at Carnegie Hall, an event that also featured Patti Smith, who contributed to the original track.

Continuing their European engagements, members of The National, excluding lead singer Matt Berninger, participated in a National Mixtape set at Berlin’s Funkhaus venue during Aaron Dessner’s PEOPLE festival. This session showcased reinterpretations of the band’s repertoire with varied guest vocalists including Bartees Strange, Angie McMahon, Ben Howard, Mina Tindle, and Tommy WÁ. The selections spanned multiple albums, reflecting both the band’s evolution and the versatility of their compositions.

As of now, The National have not announced any upcoming tour dates. However, these collaborative events, marked by rare performances and high-profile guest appearances, highlight the enduring influence and creative vitality of Aaron and Bryce Dessner as they celebrate a significant personal and professional milestone.

title: Fuerza Regida Accept Vanguard Award at 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards: ‘We’re
content:
At the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards held in Miami, Fuerza Regida received the esteemed Billboard Vanguard Award, a recognition reserved for artists who push the boundaries of musical genres and redefine industry standards. The group, rooted in San Bernardino, California, was celebrated for their groundbreaking contributions to regional Mexican music and their role in expanding its global reach.

Since forming in 2015, Fuerza Regida has forged a distinct identity by blending traditional Mexican sounds with contemporary influences, reflecting their bicultural experiences. This fusion has resonated strongly with listeners worldwide, helping the band amass over 46 million monthly Spotify listeners and accumulate more than 35 billion streams across their career. Their success is further underscored by a remarkable presence on the Billboard charts, including 16 entries on the Hot 100.

The ceremony also showcased Fuerza Regida’s dynamic stage presence through a special performance featuring the track "Pues Ya Ni Pedo" alongside Mexican-American artist Chuyin. Their energetic set, including signature white suits and thematic masks, energized the audience and underscored their innovative approach to live shows.

Billboard’s Vanguard Award honors artists who exemplify vision and innovation, spotlighting those who challenge conventional norms within the music industry. Fuerza Regida’s receipt of this award highlights their role as trailblazers in regional Mexican music, a genre traditionally confined to certain locales but now enjoying unprecedented international acclaim.

The band’s lineup, which includes Jesús Ortiz Paz (JOP), José “Pelón” García, Moisés López, Khrystian Ramos, and Samuel Jaimez, embodies a collective that honors deep cultural roots while embracing global trends. Their breakthrough collaborations, such as "El Jefe" with global superstar Shakira and "Tu Boda" with Óscar Maydon, have achieved significant chart success, including a No. 1 spot on Hot Latin Songs and high placements on worldwide rankings.

2025 marked a milestone for Fuerza Regida when their ninth studio album, 111XPANTIA, debuted at No. 2 on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart—the highest position ever attained by a Spanish-language group or duo. The album’s ascent to No. 1 on Top Latin Albums in its second week reaffirmed their commercial and critical acclaim.

Beyond streaming and chart dominance, Fuerza Regida has broken new ground in live performances. They became the first regional Mexican act to perform at Tyler, the Creator’s Camp Flog Gnaw festival and made a cultural impact at Paris Fashion Week. Their record-setting shows at Los Angeles’ Intuit Dome and sold-out concerts at iconic venues such as Madison Square Garden and the Hollywood Bowl demonstrate their expansive appeal.

Looking ahead to 2026, Fuerza Regida is set to embark on the first-ever stadium tour by a regional Mexican group in the United States, signaling the genre’s growing mainstream presence. Their participation in Billboard Latin Music Week, including a Superstar Q&A and a headline performance at the Billboard En Vivo showcase, further cements their prominence.

The awards event also honored other notable figures, such as Cristian Castro with the Lifetime Achievement Award, Rubén Blades with the Icon Award, and Rosalía’s induction into the Hall of Fame. The ceremony was broadcast live on Telemundo and Peacock, with availability across Latin America and the Caribbean.

Fuerza Regida’s Vanguard Award win encapsulates a decade of artistic evolution and perseverance. Their ability to fuse tradition with innovation and connect authentically with diverse audiences underscores their transformative influence on Latin music’s contemporary landscape, as reported by billboard.com.

title: Mark Ronson, Jessie Reyez, Corinne Bailey Rae Lead All-Star Amy Winehouse Tribut
content:
A distinguished lineup of artists gathered at London’s Roundhouse to commemorate the 20th anniversary of Amy Winehouse’s seminal album Back to Black. The event, held on a recent Wednesday, featured performances of the album’s entire tracklist, delivered by a rotating cast of vocalists accompanied by the original producers and Winehouse’s longtime band.

Mark Ronson and Salaam Remi, who co-produced the iconic 2006 record, played a central role in the concert, providing instrumental and creative support throughout the evening. Their involvement underscored the enduring influence of Back to Black on contemporary music, as they guided the musicians and singers through the album’s distinctive sound.

The tribute opened with Corinne Bailey Rae interpreting the album’s title song, setting a reflective tone for the night. Successive performances included Sasha Keable on “Just Friends,” Nia Smith on “Tears Dry on Their Own,” and Skye Newman’s take on “Addicted,” each artist bringing a fresh perspective to Winehouse’s deeply personal compositions.

Yebba and Terri Walker contributed renditions of “Love Is a Losing Game” and “Me and Mr. Jones,” respectively, while Lianne La Havas took on the sultry “You Know I’m No Good.” The evening’s program also featured Baby Rose, Jorja Smith, and the group FLO, enhancing the lineup with their distinctive vocal styles.

Notably, Jessie Reyez concluded the Back to Black segment with a powerful performance of “Rehab,” a track synonymous with Winehouse’s candid exploration of vulnerability. The choice of the Roundhouse as the venue carried additional significance, as it was the site of Winehouse’s final live performance before her passing in 2011.

To close the event, all participating artists united for a collective performance of “Valerie,” a song originally by the Zutons but famously reinterpreted by Winehouse, symbolizing her lasting impact on the music landscape.

Beyond the live concert, this tribute forms part of a broader commemoration of Amy Winehouse’s work. A deluxe edition of Back to Black has been scheduled for release, offering fans expanded content and remastered tracks. Additionally, the full concert is set to be televised on the BBC later in the month, allowing wider audiences to engage with the celebration.

This anniversary event not only honored the musical legacy of Amy Winehouse but also highlighted the collaborative spirit of artists inspired by her work. The participation of producers, original band members, and a new generation of singers demonstrated the album’s continued relevance and resonance within the music community.

While comprehensive details about the deluxe edition and broadcast remain forthcoming, the tribute concert at the Roundhouse provided a poignant reflection on Winehouse’s lasting imprint on soul and pop music two decades after Back to Black’s original release.

title: Atlanta Rapper Shawty Dred Indicted in $42M Federal SNAP Fraud Sweep
content:
Federal authorities have formally indicted Atlanta-based rapper Mercedes New, known professionally as Shawty Dred, in connection with a large-scale Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme. The indictment, announced in early October, stems from an extensive probe into a $42 million nationwide SNAP fraud operation.

The Department of Justice revealed that New is among more than 40 individuals charged in the crackdown, which targets fraudulent activities exploiting USDA assistance programs. New was apprehended in Las Vegas on October 13, following a grand jury indictment issued on October 7. Charges against him include criminal food stamp fraud, mail fraud, access device fraud, and aggravated identity theft.

Investigators allege that New orchestrated a complex scheme involving over 500 Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards issued in Georgia. Through these accounts, New is accused of unlawfully obtaining approximately $4.4 million in SNAP benefits. The case highlights extensive misuse of government resources intended for vulnerable populations.

The inquiry leading to New's arrest began in 2025 when the Georgia Department of Human Services Office of Inspector General uncovered suspicious activity linked to phone numbers associated with the rapper. These numbers reportedly contacted the SNAP interactive voice response system thousands of times, gaining unauthorized access to hundreds of SNAP accounts.

Financial records connected to New indicate that transactions on the implicated SNAP benefit cards totaled around $1.8 million. Of this, close to $635,000 was allegedly spent at Shawty Dred LLC, a retail establishment owned by New in Atlanta which had previously received SNAP authorization.

Prior to federal intervention, local law enforcement detained New in East Point, Georgia, after he allegedly solicited customers to purchase SNAP EBT cards illicitly. This arrest resulted in the recovery of several EBT cards, further substantiating the ongoing fraud investigation.

U.S. government officials have emphasized the broader implications of the case, underscoring the detrimental impact of SNAP fraud on taxpayers and families reliant on these benefits. The Department of Justice and the U.S. Department of Agriculture have collaborated extensively to dismantle such schemes and ensure accountability.

Beyond his involvement in the fraud case, Shawty Dred has cultivated a public persona as a rapper and social media figure. His music catalog includes several releases, and he has garnered attention for displaying a lavish lifestyle online, often showcasing luxury vehicles and expensive vacations. Notably, some videos have circulated showing New burning cash, an act interpreted by some as flaunting illicit gains.

The legal consequences for New could be severe. He faces a prison sentence ranging from a minimum of two years up to 20 years, contingent on the outcomes of the ongoing judicial process. Attempts to obtain statements from New or his representatives have not been successful as of this writing.

This indictment marks a significant moment in the federal government's intensified efforts to combat fraud within critical social support programs. The case serves as a cautionary reminder of the legal risks associated with exploiting public assistance funds and reflects a broader commitment to protecting resources meant for those in genuine need.

title: Queens Of The Stone Age announce 2027 ‘Perfecth’ US tour with Pixies
content:
Queens of the Stone Age have set the stage for a major US tour in 2027 as they prepare to promote their forthcoming ninth studio album, Perfecth. The band revealed a 16-date itinerary across the United States, launching their Perfecth World Tour in early May. The tour will bring the band to a variety of prominent venues, beginning at Viejas Arena in San Diego on May 1 and concluding at TD Garden in Boston on May 24.

Adding to the tour's appeal, the alternative rock pioneers Pixies are confirmed as special guests throughout the run. Pixies, who are marking their 40th anniversary with ongoing activities including tours and album reissues, will share the bill with Queens of the Stone Age, signaling a notable pairing for fans of alternative and indie rock. Supporting both acts will be Denver’s alternative hip-hop group Wheelchair Sports Camp, who will perform at all dates.

The announcement came just days before Perfecth’s official release on October 30 via Matador Records, marking the band’s first new album since 2023’s In Times New Roman…. Queens of the Stone Age frontman Josh Homme described the album as a collection of diverse sounds that explore complex themes such as love, lust, and the wisdom gained from human folly, highlighting the record’s deliberate eclecticism.

Prior to the full album drop, the band has unveiled several singles—Easy Street, Insignificant Other, and Where The Goth Girls At?—with the latter making its live debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in late October. This exposure adds momentum to the upcoming tour and album release.

Queens of the Stone Age have maintained a rigorous touring schedule through 2026, which includes supporting Foo Fighters on their Take Cover stadium tour across North America. Their extensive itinerary also features international performances spanning Iceland, Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, and New Zealand. Early in 2027, the band will return to Mexico City for a significant co-headlining show with Interpol.

Meanwhile, Pixies have been active throughout 2026 with anniversary celebrations encompassing UK and European tours alongside the reissue of seminal albums Bossanova and Trompe Le Monde. Their latest studio effort, The Night The Zombies Came, was released in 2024 featuring new bassist Emma Richardson. Guitarist Joey Santiago has indicated the band continues to develop new material, promising further creative output.

Ticket sales for the Queens of the Stone Age 2027 US tour are scheduled to begin with an artist pre-sale on October 28, followed by a general public sale on October 29. Fans interested in accessing the pre-sale must register by October 25. This marks the initial leg of the Perfecth World Tour, with additional shows anticipated but yet to be announced.

The tour’s itinerary covers a mix of major metropolitan areas across the country, including stops in Los Angeles, Oakland, Seattle, Portland, Detroit, and several Midwest and East Coast cities. This expansive route reflects the band’s sustained popularity and commitment to reaching a broad American audience.

As Queens of the Stone Age prepare to embark on this campaign, the combination of a new album, a high-profile tour, and the partnership with Pixies represents a significant moment in the current rock landscape. Fans can anticipate a dynamic live experience as these influential groups bring their distinct sounds and legacies to stages nationwide.

title: ‘Elsinore’ to Receive Gotham Legacy Tribute in Honor of Ian Charleson (EXCLUSIVE
content:
The Gotham Film & Media Institute has announced it will present a Legacy Tribute to the film ‘Elsinore’ during the upcoming Gotham Film Awards set for November 30 at Cipriani Wall Street in New York City. The tribute recognizes the film’s portrayal of the late actor Ian Charleson, celebrating his enduring influence on stage and screen.

Ian Charleson, who passed away in 1990, is perhaps best remembered for his role in the Academy Award-winning film ‘Chariots of Fire.’ ‘Elsinore’ revisits his compelling story, focusing on his courageous final months when he was diagnosed with AIDS while preparing to perform one of theater’s most demanding roles, Hamlet.

The film’s narrative centers on Charleson's resilience and artistic dedication during this challenging period. It explores how he faced his diagnosis with honesty and grace, channeling his experience into a powerful stage performance that resonated deeply with audiences and colleagues alike. This portrayal sheds light on the personal and communal dimensions of his journey amid the early years of the HIV epidemic.

Andrew Scott stars as Charleson, delivering a performance that captures the complexity and strength of the actor’s final chapter. Supporting cast members include Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, and Joe Locke. Colman plays Dr. Margaret Johnson, a pioneering physician who established one of the first dedicated HIV clinics and treated Charleson and other gay men during this critical period.

Directed by Simon Stone and written by Stephen Beresford, ‘Elsinore’ has already attracted significant attention on the festival circuit. It debuted at the Telluride Film Festival and was featured in the Special Presentations section at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it earned the International People’s Choice Award, signaling strong audience acclaim.

The film’s limited theatrical release begins on November 20, with wider distribution planned through the Thanksgiving holiday and into December. Its production involved collaboration among Studiocanal, LD Entertainment, Lucky Red, and Magnolia Mae Films.

The Gotham Film Awards ceremony will also honor other notable achievements in cinema this year. Among the tributes, the film ‘Michael’ will receive a musical tribute, while ‘La Bola Negra’ is set for the Vanguard Tribute. Esteemed director Danny Boyle is slated to be recognized for his work on ‘Ink,’ and the animation studio Laika will be celebrated with an anniversary tribute.

Nominees for the 36th annual Gotham Film Awards are scheduled for announcement on October 27. The event continues to highlight films and talent that push creative boundaries and bring impactful stories to audiences.

By honoring ‘Elsinore’ with a Legacy Tribute, the Gotham Film & Media Institute not only commemorates Ian Charleson’s remarkable career and personal bravery but also acknowledges the film’s role in illuminating a significant cultural moment. The tribute underscores the lasting power of performance art to inspire and heal, particularly when confronting life’s most profound challenges.

title: From LISA to Miley Cyrus, John Mayer & More, Which New Music Release Is Your Fav
content:
This week’s New Music Friday brings a rich variety of releases that span genres and global influences, setting the tone for the next wave of playlists and listening experiences. At the forefront is LISA, the BLACKPINK member, who has launched her Press Play EP. The six-track bilingual project arrives just ahead of her upcoming Las Vegas residency scheduled for mid-November. Notable within the EP is the Hot 100-charting single “SaWaDiKa,” alongside “Tarantino” and the track “Cobra,” which uniquely incorporates elements from a Missy Elliott and Timbaland classic.

In the R&B and hip-hop realms, two major albums have captured attention. John Legend’s Muse marks his first full-length collaboration with producer Pharrell Williams. This partnership originated from their earlier work on a 2025 Grammy-winning track, highlighting a new chapter in both artists’ discographies. Meanwhile, Yung Miami has released Watch Dis, her debut solo album after nearly a decade of success as part of City Girls. This project follows the momentum generated by her breakout hit “Spend Dat” earlier this year.

Country music also sees notable activity with Kacey Musgraves previewing Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes. This 16-track expansion builds on the themes and sound of her earlier 2024 release, offering a breezy, southwestern vibe exemplified by the single “Weekend In Texas.” Adding to the diversity, British DJ Sammy Virji surprised fans with his sophomore album Open Late, an energetic project largely crafted during his touring schedule.

The breadth of new music extends through numerous other artists and genres. Claud’s Me and the Music, Anderson .Paak and Cordae’s collaborative album Heavy Is the Crown, and Halle’s deluxe edition of Love?… Or Something Like It represent just a portion of this week’s output. Rap, alternative, and soul artists such as Brakence, Toosii, Yeat, Samara Joy, and Che Noir also contribute new full-length projects. Noteworthy reissues include My Chemical Romance’s 20th anniversary deluxe edition of The Black Parade.

Singles further diversify the playlist landscape. Miley Cyrus has released “Cold Blood,” a previously unreleased mid-2010s demo featured on the soundtrack for Netflix’s third season of Nobody Wants This. Country artists Megan Moroney and Carly Pearce have introduced new tracks “Say When” and “Not Falling Out,” respectively, with Pearce collaborating alongside Max McNown. Meanwhile, John Mayer has stepped into the spotlight with “Tom and Jerry,” debuting under his newly established Sob Rock Records label.

Other singles from emerging and established artists enrich the musical offerings. Dominic Fike teases his upcoming album with “Pangea,” and Snoh Aalegra continues to promote Legendary Love through new material. Additional releases come from Xavi, ATEEZ, King Princess, Timothée Chalamet with Hans Zimmer, Lake Street Dive, Jxdn, keshi, and an international array including Neton Vega and Fuerza Regida.

Hip-hop and rap scenes are represented by singles from artists like Myke Towers, French Montana, Skepta, and Wiz Khalifa, further highlighting the genre’s global reach. Collaborations and solo tracks alike contribute to a dynamic and varied musical week, while artists such as Girlset, Mannywellz, Olamide, and Fousheé add even more layers to the sonic tapestry.

This week’s releases underscore the evolving nature of contemporary music consumption, where genres intersect and artists innovate through collaboration and experimentation. From high-profile debuts to surprise drops, the musical landscape offers something for a wide spectrum of listeners, reflecting both established stars and rising talents.

As these new projects circulate, audiences are invited to engage and select their favorites, shaping the soundtracks of upcoming weeks. The diversity of styles and influences showcased this New Music Friday not only highlights individual artistic journeys but also exemplifies the rich, interconnected fabric of today’s music industry.

title: Cristian Castro Accepts the Billboard Lifetime Achievement Award ‘In the Name of
content:
At the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards held at Miami's James L. Knight Center, Cristian Castro was bestowed with the prestigious Billboard Lifetime Achievement Award. The ceremony, broadcast live on Telemundo and Peacock, celebrated the singer's remarkable career that has significantly influenced Latin music over three decades.

Receiving the award from Mexican actress Jacqueline Bracamontes, Castro reflected on the enduring themes that have defined his artistry, particularly the power of romantic love and poetry. Emphasizing these as fundamental human experiences, he framed his musical journey as deeply intertwined with these elements, which have inspired much of his repertoire.

Castro’s career achievements include multiple chart-topping hits on Billboard’s Hot Latin Songs, such as "Amor," "Azul," and "Nunca Voy a Olvidarte." His debut album, Agua Nueva, launched in the early 1990s, quickly established him as a rising star within Latin pop, reaching No. 2 on the Top Latin Pop Albums chart. His tribute album Viva El Príncipe, honoring José José, also garnered critical and commercial success, spending seven weeks at No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart in 2011.

With over 12 million records sold worldwide, Castro has maintained a strong connection with audiences through his Nada Solo Éxitos Tour, which includes performances in iconic venues like Mexico City’s Auditorio Nacional and New York’s Madison Square Garden. His influence extends beyond his music, recognized by Billboard as pivotal in shaping global appreciation for Latin pop and romantic genres.

During the awards ceremony, Castro delivered a special live performance alongside Mexican-American duo Ha*Ash, debuting their collaboration "Antes Que Te Cases." This marked a celebratory moment in the evening, highlighting both his legacy and ongoing creative vitality.

The Billboard Lifetime Achievement Award is reserved for artists whose careers have elevated Latin music on the world stage and whose artistic and personal contributions have left a lasting imprint on the genre’s development. Past honorees include some of Latin music’s most iconic figures such as Carlos Santana, Marco Antonio Solís, and Maná.

The 2026 ceremony also recognized other influential artists, with Rubén Blades receiving the Billboard Icon Award, Rosalía inducted into the Billboard Hall of Fame, and Fuerza Regida honored with the Billboard Vanguard Award. These accolades underscore the event’s role in acknowledging both longstanding contributions and emerging trends within Latin music.

Cristian Castro’s recognition reflects not only his commercial success but also his artistic dedication to themes of love and emotional expression, which continue to resonate with fans across generations. His acceptance speech and performance encapsulated the spirit of the evening, blending reverence for tradition with contemporary collaboration.

As Latin music continues to expand its global influence, figures like Castro remain central to its narrative, bridging past achievements with future possibilities. The Lifetime Achievement Award cements his status as a seminal figure within this evolving cultural landscape.

title: FLO, Jorja Smith, Skye Newman & more star at Amy Winehouse tribute concert
content:
A commemorative concert honoring Amy Winehouse’s landmark album Back To Black took place on October 21 at London’s Roundhouse, drawing an array of acclaimed contemporary vocalists and key figures from Winehouse’s original production team. The event marked two decades since the release of the album that would come to define Winehouse’s enduring influence on modern music.

The concert featured performances of the entire Back To Black album, led by its original producers Mark Ronson and Salaam Remi, alongside longtime collaborators including Winehouse’s musical director Dale Davis, producers Paul O’Duffy and P*nut, and music executive Darcus Beese OBE. The live backing was provided by the Amy Winehouse Band, aiming to recreate the sound and spirit of the original recordings.

A diverse lineup of guest artists each took on individual songs from the album. Among the featured vocalists were FLO, Jorja Smith, Skye Newman, Baby Rose, Corinne Bailey Rae, Jessie Reyez, Nia Smith, Sasha Keable, Terri Walker, and Yebba. The concert culminated in a group performance of "Valerie," a track famously covered by Winehouse, originally by The Zutons, showcasing the collaborative atmosphere of the tribute.

This event not only celebrated the album’s musical achievements but also highlighted the ongoing cultural resonance of Winehouse’s work. The Back To Black album originally debuted at number three on the UK charts before ascending to number one, ultimately becoming the best-selling album in the UK for 2007 with over 4.6 million sales to date according to the Official Charts Company.

The album’s success was further cemented by its recognition at the Grammy Awards, where Winehouse secured five awards including Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance among others, reflecting both critical acclaim and popular impact.

In conjunction with the concert, a special reissue campaign was launched by UMR/Island featuring a 3LP clear vinyl and 3CD set of Back To Black, along with limited edition 1LP pressings of the original album. These reissues include previously unreleased demos, rare B-sides, live recordings from Amsterdam’s Paradiso venue, and unseen photography by Mischa Richter and Alex Lake, complemented by new liner notes from Ronson and Remi.

The tribute concert is scheduled for broadcast on BBC Two and available on BBC iPlayer on October 24, forming part of a broader BBC programming initiative celebrating Winehouse’s legacy. Additional commemorations include broadcasts on BBC Radio 2 and BBC Sounds, as well as a dedicated special on BBC Radio 6 Music.

The Roundhouse itself holds historical significance in Winehouse’s career, having hosted her performances during the BBC Electric Proms in 2006. Returning to this venue for the tribute underlines the ongoing connection between Winehouse’s music and the British live music scene.

Producers and collaborators reflected on Winehouse’s unique artistry and the passionate dedication behind the album’s creation. They emphasized her distinctive blend of talent, emotional honesty, and creative spirit that continues to inspire new generations of artists and fans worldwide.

This tribute underscores the lasting power of Back To Black not only as a commercial success but as a cultural milestone that continues to influence contemporary music and maintain a devoted global audience.
